name: Vikas Varma Pokala
title: Software Engineer | Full Stack
summary: Software engineer with 2+ years of production experience building backend and full-stack systems across healthcare and enterprise platforms. Experienced with Java/Spring Boot, Node.js/TypeScript, Go, React, GraphQL, Kafka, and real-time systems, with work spanning products used by 250+ doctors, a healthcare platform used at the University of Toronto, and TELUS Marketplace.

skills.Backend: Spring Boot, Node.js, Express.js, REST APIs, GraphQL, Kafka consumers, WebSockets, Microservices
skills.Cloud / DevOps: AWS (S3, KMS, CloudWatch), GCP, Docker, Firebase
skills.Auth & Security: JWT, OAuth 2.0, Firebase Auth, encryption at rest, rate limiting

experience.title: Full Stack Developer – AI & Web Applications

project_blocks.project: Institution Digital Systems — Website, Email, and College Portal
bullets: Architecting and building a role-based college portal with shared sign-in for students, faculty, and administrators using React, Node.js/Express with TypeScript, and Java/Spring Boot; implementing attendance workflows for user mapping, daily entry, corrections, permission checks, and administrative review.

Building backend services around 12-factor principles, including environment-based configuration, stateless API processes, clear service boundaries, and deployment-ready application design to improve maintainability and operational consistency.

Building custom AI agents and internal workflow tools for college operations, including accounting, reception, and administrative processes, while also modernizing the institution website, domain, and official email systems.
Joined as backend engineer when the product had ~100 active doctors; over six months, the platform scaled to 250+ doctors across Toronto clinics on the back of the work below.
Replaced AWS Transcribe with Soniox for live transcription, ran both providers in parallel for ~3 months, reduced transcription cost from ~$1.00/hr to ~$0.10/hr, and added support for 40+ languages.
Reduced AI note-generation time from ~60s to ~20–30s by removing redundant backend steps and optimizing regex post-processing; added token streaming for progressive note rendering.

Implemented JWT-based service authentication, OAuth 2.0 sign-in, encryption at rest for notes and audio, and per-endpoint rate limiting as part of a broader security hardening effort for HIPAA-aligned workflows.

Integrated Recall.ai for Google Meet, Zoom, Teams, and Webex sessions, processing continuous transcript chunks via webhooks with ordering and retry handling, then streaming updates to the frontend over WebSockets.

Built a partner-facing transcription and note-generation platform with a separate API surface, API-key management dashboard, usage tracking by hours and notes for billing, and developer documentation with sample code.
Owned the GraphQL signup flow coordinating organization, customer, billing, password, terms, and email-confirmation processes across Java/Spring Boot microservices with cross-service error handling.
Built a reusable email-template API in a Java/Spring Boot Kafka consumer, added new notification types, and resolved templating issues used across multiple teams.
Developed Go + GraphQL resolvers in the BFF layer between the React frontend and Java microservices, aggregating backend responses and exposing only the fields required by the frontend.
Served as the sole backend developer for a Node.js/MongoDB pre-visit assessment platform used by 30+ doctors at the University of Toronto, while also building the patient-facing React experience.
Designed a configurable form engine supporting multiple question types, answer-based branching, and scoring, allowing administrators to manage assessments without code changes.
Built a passwordless assessment flow using unique email links and server-side state, allowing patients to pause questionnaires and resume on another device without creating an account.

Integrated OpenAI for structured clinical summaries with per-form prompts, configurable summary length, failure handling for rate limits, malformed responses, and timeouts, plus per-doctor retention policies.
